conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence is a cross-principal authority failure in an AI-assisted privileged support workflow. A person interacting with the recovery system had authority to make requests concerning their own account state, but the workflow allowed an attacker-supplied email address and recovery request to alter the separately governed authentication state of another identifiable account holder. The material failure is not that the AI support tool existed or that an attacker could converse with it; it is that the surrounding recovery pathway failed to preserve the account-holder boundary before issuing a credential-reset capability. Meta's statement that the support tool itself worked as intended is preserved: the evidenced defect was in a separate verification code path adjacent to the AI-assisted workflow. Account entitlement, recovery-signal binding and prior verification failures are retained. The separate code-path defect is not recast as an LLM jailbreak; potentially affected users are not all confirmed takeovers.

Meta's statement that the support tool itself worked as intended is preserved: the evidenced defect was in a separate verification code path adjacent to the AI-assisted workflow. Account entitlement, recovery-signal binding and prior verification failures are retained. The separate code-path defect is not recast as an LLM jailbreak; potentially affected users are not all confirmed takeovers. The account-autonomy and secure-operation outcomes are Not aligned.
